correctness.rationale: The 256 distinct eight-windows are verified for both explicit cycles. Each length-eight factor is unique, giving a capacity bound of 32 and forcing any equality case to be one of eight residue classes. The lower example has a complete missing seven-factor certificate for every such class and an explicit 33-point cover; the other example has an explicit 32-point cover. Orders 1,2,4 are covered by a complete finite enumeration of 495 balanced order-four candidates with all 16 qualifying necklaces and attractor checks. Executable finite certificates were independently replayed; no inference from small random experiments is used.

value.rationale: This identifies the first power-of-two de Bruijn order at which two necklaces exhibit distinct exact circular string-attractor sizes, revealing a concrete obstruction between optimal sharp-window coverage and full-factor coverage. The problem is motivated by the known lower bound and explicit questions on optimal de Bruijn attractors, not by arbitrary parameter slicing.
